entries.core_move: Identify whether a continuous-time signal is periodic or aperiodic by testing for a finite repeating period and linking aperiodicity to the need for Fourier-transform analysis.
Interpret an aperiodic signal as the infinite-period limit of a periodic extension to connect Fourier-series harmonics with the Fourier-transform viewpoint.
Compute the Fourier-series frequency spacing $\omega$_0 = 2*pi/T and interpret how it shrinks toward continuous frequency as the period grows without bound.
Interpret continuous frequency as the variable that replaces discrete harmonic indices when the Fourier-series period grows without bound.
Apply the Fourier transform definition to convert an aperiodic continuous-time signal $x(t)$ into its continuous-frequency spectrum $X(j \omega)$.
Apply the inverse Fourier transform to reconstruct an aperiodic continuous-time signal $x(t)$ from its continuous-frequency spectrum $X(j \omega)$.
Interpret Fourier transform pair notation by matching $x(t)$ and $X(j \omega)$ to the forward and inverse transforms that connect a time-domain signal with its spectrum.
